st: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in the beans and their liquid. Cook 3 minutes until hot.
Add the cold rice and break up any clumps with a spoon.
Pour in the Salsa Lizano, salt and pepper. Stir for 5 minutes until the rice is evenly speckled brown and everything is hot.
Stir in half the cilantro and use the rest to garnish. Serve at breakfast with eggs and sour cream.
Rinse the rice, then simmer with [[3 cups]] water, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[1 tbsp]] oil, covered, for 18 minutes. Rest 5 minutes.
Warm the beans in a pot with half the garlic and the cumin for 10 minutes.
Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt, the remaining garlic and the juice of one lime.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 5 minutes per side until it reaches 165°F (74°C). Rest and slice.
Fry the plantain slices in [[1/4 cup]] oil for 2 minutes per side until deep golden. Drain.
Toss the cabbage and tomato with lime juice and a pinch of salt for the simple salad.
Fry the eggs. Plate the rice, beans, chicken, plantains, salad and egg together.

ing: beef shank or chuck with bones
st: Put the beef, onion, garlic, half the cilantro, salt and water in a large pot. Bring to a boil.
Skim the foam off the top. Reduce to a low simmer and cover.
Cook for 90 minutes until the beef is very tender.
Add the yuca and carrots and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the potatoes, corn and chayote and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the plantains and simmer 10 more minutes until all vegetables are tender.
Taste the broth and adjust the salt. Chop the remaining cilantro and scatter on top.
Serve the broth first as soup, then the meat and vegetables on a plate with rice.
Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper.
Heat the oil in a wide pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken for 5 minutes per side, then remove.
In the same pot, cook the onion, bell pepper and carrots for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and turmeric for 1 minute.
Stir in the rice and cook 2 minutes to coat it in oil.
Add the broth, Salsa Lizano and [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil and nestle the chicken in.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 25 minutes until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Scatter the peas on top, cover, and rest 10 minutes. Fluff and sprinkle with cilantro.
Mix the tomatoes, onion, cilantro, juice of 2 limes and [[1/2 tsp]] salt for the pico de gallo. Set aside.
Put the pork belly cubes in a skillet with the water and [[1/2 tsp]] salt. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Cook uncovered for 15 minutes until the water evaporates and the fat starts to render.
Keep frying for 10 more minutes, turning, until crisp and golden and the pork reaches 145°F (63°C) or higher. Drain on paper towels.
Warm the beans in a pot with the garlic for 5 minutes. Season with a little salt.
Layer rice and beans in 4 bowls. Add the pork and then a big spoonful of pico.
Squeeze lime over the top, add hot sauce, and serve with the tortilla chips.
Drain the soaked beans and put them in a large pot with the water. Bring to a boil.
Simmer partly covered for 75 minutes until very soft. Skim foam if needed.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper for 6 minutes. Add the garlic and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the vegetables and [[1/4 cup]] cilantro to the beans, along with the salt and pepper.
Simmer 10 more minutes. Blend the soup with an immersion blender until smooth, or leave half the beans whole.
Taste and adjust the salt.
Ladle into bowls and add 1 egg to each. Sprinkle with the remaining cilantro and squeeze lime over.

ing: 12-inch squares, or use corn husks or foil
st: Simmer the pork in water with the onion, [[1 tsp]] salt and garlic for 60 minutes until very tender. Shred it and save [[1 cup]] of the broth.
Cook the tomato and pork with the Salsa Lizano and the reserved broth for 5 minutes into a moist filling.
Mix the masa harina, [[1 tsp]] salt, lard and [[2 cups]] warm broth into a smooth, soft dough like thick mashed potatoes.
Pass the banana leaves over a flame or hot pan for a few seconds until shiny and flexible. Cut away the stiff rib.
Spread [[1/3 cup]] of masa in the center of each leaf. Top with pork, a spoon of partly cooked rice, potato and pepper strips.
Fold the leaf over the filling to enclose, fold the ends in, and tie with twine in a rectangular packet.
Boil the packets in a large pot of water, covered, for 90 minutes until the masa is firm and pulls cleanly from the leaf.
Drain and rest 10 minutes. Unwrap and eat hot.
Cut off the plantain ends, slit the peel along its length, and peel. Cut into 1-inch thick rounds.
Heat the oil to 325°F (160°C) in a deep skillet.
Fry the rounds for 3 minutes per side until pale gold. Remove.
Using a flat glass or plate, press each piece between parchment sheets to about 1/4 inch thick.
Stir the water, [[1/2 tsp]] salt and crushed garlic. Dip each flattened piece for a moment.
Reheat the oil to 375°F (190°C). Fry the pieces for 2 minutes per side until crisp and golden.
Drain and sprinkle with [[1/2 tsp]] salt. Warm the black beans, mash them, and serve on top or alongside.

ing: very fresh sea bass or snapper, in 1/2-inch cubes
st: Buy very fresh fish labeled safe for raw use and keep it cold. Cut it into 1/2-inch cubes.
Put the fish in a glass bowl and add the salt.
Pour the lime juice over the fish until it is covered.
Cover and refrigerate for 20 to 30 minutes, stirring once, until the fish turns opaque and white throughout.
Meanwhile, dice the onion, bell pepper and chili and chop the cilantro. Rinse the onion in cold water for 1 minute to soften the bite.
Stir the vegetables and cilantro into the fish with the pepper.
Taste and add more salt or lime if needed. Serve cold right away with chips.
Put the carrots, onion, celery and water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the vegetables are completely soft.
Add the vinegar, sugar, mustard, cumin, turmeric, pepper, salt and soy sauce and simmer 5 minutes.
Blend everything very smooth in a blender, taking care with the hot liquid.
Strain through a fine sieve back into the pot, pressing out all the liquid.
Whisk in the cornstarch mixture and simmer 3 minutes until lightly thickened.
Cool and pour into a clean jar. Keep in the fridge for up to 2 weeks and shake before using.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking pan.
Whisk together the flour, baking powder and salt.
Beat the egg yolks with [[3/4 cup]] sugar for 3 minutes until pale and thick. Mix in the [[1/2 cup]] milk and [[1 tsp]] vanilla. Fold in the flour.
In a clean bowl, beat the egg whites until foamy, then add [[1/4 cup]] sugar and beat to stiff peaks. Gently fold into the batter.
Pour into the pan and bake 25 minutes until golden and a toothpick comes out clean. Cool 15 minutes.
Poke the cake all over with a fork. Whisk the evaporated milk, condensed milk and [[1/2 cup]] cream and pour slowly over the cake.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight so the cake soaks up the milk.
Whip [[1 cup]] cream with the powdered sugar and [[1 tsp]] vanilla to soft peaks. Spread on top, dust with cinnamon and serve cold.
